title: Post-first-second residual emptying fraction did not establish added chronic-phlegm prediction across separate NHANES samples
abstract: In 2,331 NHANES 2007–2008 adults aged 40–79, we trained weighted logistic models for chronic phlegm using demographics, smoking, adiposity and standard spirometry. Adding D=(FVC−FEV3)/(FVC−FEV1) worsened source PSU-grouped cross-validation. Frozen evaluation in 2,188 separately sampled 2011–2012 adults changed log loss by +0.00007977 (target stratified-PSU 95% interval −0.00006330 to +0.00022799; source-and-target refit interval −0.00017017 to +0.00088771) and AUROC by −0.000506. No stable incremental benefit was established. D is algebraically recoverable from FEV3/FVC and FEV1/FVC, and the public summaries need not describe one maneuver. This is a negative representation test, not evidence against small-airway physiology.
